chapter: Taking New Orleans musicians on the road
title: How New Orleans jazz spread north and Oliver's influence
summary: Billy says the beat reached other places only when New Orleans men spread out, Chicago first. Local musicians were puzzled, crowds of players listened at the Royal Garden, and the traveling shows gave many their start.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Another fellow that called him. Yes, there's a later one. I wonder, did you notice much difference in the bands, the early bands, between the New
Orleans fellows and the other musicians up north or other places in the south? Was there a different beat? Oh, yes.

Well, you know, say the jazz originated, that kind of ragtime and all they called it then, started in New Orleans. I wondered if you found that same kind of music up north or other places too? No, no, no. No, no.

They didn't any take it up until those fellows from New Orleans began to spread out up this way. Chicago being the easiest way north, and most of them came here first. Yes. And then from here they branched out to Philadelphia, New York and places.

And we found too that there are a lot of musicians that were already here that didn't know that, didn't have that beat, didn't understand what it was all about. A lot of them were puzzled. I wouldn't, some of them argued they wouldn't play. That's not a lot of junk, you know. But they all come to it. Yeah, Joe Oliver, he was the one that started it here almost. Him and Johnny Dodds and them.
Yes. That's why at the Lincoln Garden, I mean the Royal Garden, they would be so crowded, the musicians around looking and listening and learning.

Joe Oliver and them started it. Well, there was a couple of fellows around these other nightclubs too, like Jimmy Noon, Freddie, what was his name? Keppard maybe. Keppard. Freddie Keppard, yes. Did you ever work with him?
He traveled with us for a while. Oh, he did? Well, I didn't clap, Freddie Keppard, yes.
I never knew him, but I know his brother is still living there, a very nice guitar player. He plays guitar. Louis Keppard.
Because we were about the only ones that had a show down there, didn't we?
Yeah. Well, traveling shows would go anywhere out of the race of New Orleans and certainly.

And any time the musicians would, some of them would get hot-headed or something like that. We would, and we'd show, go back and show in New Orleans. Well, then we'd bring new ones out. Yes. Then eventually, when they come to the centers and they want to come back, we take them back. Always party friendly. Yeah.
Quite a few of them got their start with us. That is, the traveling start in a way. They were playing music.
